newsitem.title: GERMANY: Grain harvest in full swing across Germany.
newsitem.headline: Grain harvest in full swing across Germany.

text.p: Grain harvesting is in full swing in Germany, where farmers hope to finish work by the end of August, farm sources said on Monday.
Farmers in southern and western regions, where the harvest was mostly complete, were already planting some winter rapeseed, but the bulk of this crop would be sown next month.
Regions further north had finished winter barley, some winter rye and wheat as well as rapeseed.
But export regions in the north were still in the middle of the rye, wheat and triticale harvests, with oats and spring barley still outstanding and maize harvesting at least 10 days off.
The DWD national meteorological office said the weather would stay mostly sunny and dry throughout the country this week and this should help secure good quality.
Wheat qualities were better than previously expected, albeit below last year's yields and protein contents.
Hagberg falling numbers were high at 200 seconds on average.
The ZMP farm price office made the following comments on wheat crops in western German regions --
Schleswig-Holstein yields were between seven and 10 tonnes per hectare (tph), proteins varied and Hagberg numbers were fine.
Westphalian-Lippe proteins were mostly too low for baking, with counts in Rhineland-Palatinate also weak.
North Rhine-Westphalian wheat was around, or just below, 12 percent protein, with falling numbers above 250 seconds.
Saar region protein contents were between 10 and 13 percent and farmers in Hesse state also reported good qualities between eight and 14 percent protein.
Bavaria said proteins were weaker than last year but yields were average.
South Baden also reported an average yield and protein contents between nine and 12.5 percent.
Problems with low rye falling numbers persisted, disqualifying large parts of the crop for baking, while the early winter barley crop had shown good yields and qualities.
